ai.instructions: Use these tools to answer questions about UK companies, their officers and their ownership, using Companies House data. A company number is 8 characters — eight digits, or two letters followed by six digits, e.g. OC394454. Search by name first, then pass the returned company number or officer id to the detail tools. Companies House does not verify what companies file, so report what the register says and never present it as verification, a credit check or clearance. An officer's date of birth is published as month and year only. Ceased and resigned entries stay on the register, so check the ceased or resigned date before describing anyone as current. Take counts from the register's own totals — total, active_count, resigned_count, ceased_count — rather than from the length of a list, because a tool returns one page. An absent record is a fact about the company, not a failure — say a company has no charges or no insolvency history rather than reporting an error. The disqualified directors register is a separate register with its own ids, so it can only be searched by name; an officer id from search-officers or get-officers will not resolve there. Different people share names, so always carry the caveat that a name match is not proof of identity.
